newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: EIN says pioneers video streaming on web sites.
newsitem.headline: EIN says pioneers video streaming on web sites.

text.p: The European Information Network Inc (EIN), an Internet publisher, said on Wednesday it planned to launch a streamed video news broadcast over its Russia Today web site.
Privately-owned EIN, headquartered in Prague, said it would produce its first broadcast on Monday and that this would be the first of its kind in Europe.
The five-minute newscast, which draws on various news sources, will be streamed from the Web server and will be available on demand without having to be downloaded before being viewed.
"This represents some of the best of where the Internet is going," EIN chief executive David Rothstein told reporters.
Video over the Internet has long been a problem because of the difficulties of handling the relatively large amounts of data that video involves.
Streaming involves sending packets of video in a stream from a server. Visitors to the EIN site can watch the video through a player produced by Vivo Software of the U.S.
The company employs about 30 people and has three main online publications, covering Central Europe, Russia and China. It is funded by advertising and online merchandising.
